unit-ww501-syn.title: Wordly Wise · Lesson 1 Synonyms & Antonyms
unit-ww501-syn.source: Vocabulary Unit 1: Synonyms and Antonyms — Wordly Wise Lesson 1 study sheet (Drive)

summary.text: The class study sheet for Lesson 1, built around one synonym and one antonym for each of the 15 vocabulary words — the same list unit-ww501 already covers, tested a different way. The sheet itself says the unit test draws directly from these pairs.

why.text: A synonym or antonym is really a small proof that you understand a word's meaning, not just its spelling — you have to know what "accustom" means before you can spot "ignore" as its opposite. That is exactly the kind of recall a unit test checks.

objectives.text: State a synonym and, where the sheet gives one, an antonym for each Lesson 1 word.
Recognize a word's synonym or antonym among other Lesson 1 vocabulary.

parentNote.text: Built from "Lesson 1 synonyms and antonyms.pdf," which says outright that the unit test draws from this list. The source is a 3-column table flattened by text extraction, and two words — jostle and pedestrian — come out with no antonym at all (checked twice, same result both times, so this reads as the sheet leaving them blank rather than a misread). Nothing is invented for those gaps: only their synonyms are tested. "Patient" carries synonyms for both of its senses — tolerant/composed as an adjective, victim/sufferer as the noun for someone under a doctor's care — and only the adjective sense had a antonym given, so that is the only one tested.

nextUp.text: The cards first, since a synonym only means something once the base word is solid — then the questions.

cards.def:
**Synonyms: adapt, adjust. Antonym: neglect, ignore.**
• If you're accustomed to a sound, you stop noticing it; if you neglect or ignore it, you never got used to it at all.

**Synonyms: attentive, watchful. Antonym: inattentive.**
• An alert lookout is attentive; an inattentive one misses what is right in front of them.

**Synonyms: set, give. Antonym: reject.**
• A teacher can assign extra credit, or a student can reject it and turn it down.

**Synonyms: stir, shift. Antonym: oppose.**
• A team that won't budge on a plan is refusing to shift; a team that opposes it is fighting it outright.

**Synonyms: sturdy, well-built. Antonym: slight.**
• A burly wrestler and a slight, narrow-framed gymnast are built in opposite ways.

**Synonyms: partner, friend. Antonym: foe.**
• A companion travels beside you; a foe works against you.

**Synonyms: together, cooperative. Antonym: disagreeable.**
• Compatible roommates get along easily; disagreeable ones argue over everything.

**Synonyms: idea, notion. Antonym: fact.**
• A concept is still just an idea being worked out; a fact has already been proven true.

**Synonyms: divert, sidetrack. Antonym: focus.**
• Noise in the hallway can distract you from homework; closing the door helps you focus instead.

**Synonyms: bump, knock, shove.**
• A crowded hallway is full of jostling — everyone bumping and knocking into everyone else.

**Synonyms: compliant, dutiful. Antonym: defiant.**
• An obedient dog sits the first time you ask; a defiant one plants its paws and refuses.

**Synonyms: barrier, hurdle. Antonym: advantage.**
• A locked gate is an obstacle in your way; a shortcut is an advantage that helps you along.

**Synonyms: tolerant, composed. Antonym: complains.**
• As an adjective, patient means willing to wait calmly — the opposite of someone who complains at every delay. Patient is also a noun: victim and sufferer are close synonyms for the person a doctor is treating.

**Synonyms: walker, hiker.**
• A pedestrian crosses at the light on foot, the way a walker or a hiker covers ground — no engine involved.

**Synonyms: quit, stop, turn in, call it a day. Antonym: rise, wake.**
• You retire to bed when you are tired and ready to stop for the night; you rise or wake once you are done sleeping.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of accustom?
questions.hint: Accustom is built on custom — a habit, something you do so often you stop thinking about it.
steps: Accustom means to get used to something until you stop noticing it.
Its opposite is refusing to give it any attention at all.
Adapt means the same as accustom, so it cannot be the opposite.
The answer is ignore.

ex.main: **Ignore.** Accustom is about getting so used to something that you stop noticing it. To ignore is to give it no attention in the first place — the sheet pairs them as opposites.
ex.tip: Adapt is a SYNONYM of accustom, put there to catch a fast read. Neglect works as an antonym too.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of alert?
questions.hint: One of these means the SAME as the word, not the opposite. Read the question again before you pick.
steps: Alert means paying close attention to what is going on around you.
Watchful means the same thing, so it is not the opposite.
Disagreeable and slight describe other things entirely — temper and build.
The answer is inattentive.

ex.main: **Inattentive.** Alert is about attention being switched on; inattentive is that same attention switched off. The other two are about temper and body build, not noticing.
ex.tip: Alert comes from the Italian all’erta — “on the lookout.”

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of assign?
questions.hint: Assign shares its root with signature — it is about marking something as someone’s to do.
steps: To assign is to hand a job to someone.
Give means the same thing, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is refusing to take the job on.
The answer is reject.

ex.main: **Reject.** Assigning hands a task over; rejecting is turning that handover down. Oppose is fighting an idea, which is a different move.
ex.tip: Give is a SYNONYM of assign. Watch for those.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of budge?
questions.hint: One of these means the SAME as the word, not the opposite. Read the question again before you pick.
steps: To budge is to move even a little.
Shift means the same, so it is not the opposite.
Someone who will not budge is standing against the whole idea.
The answer is oppose.

ex.main: **Oppose.** Budging is giving a little ground; opposing is standing against it entirely. Reject turns down an offer, which is narrower than opposing an idea.
ex.tip: Budge comes from the French bouger, to stir.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of burly?
questions.hint: One of these means the SAME as the word, not the opposite. Read the question again before you pick.
steps: Burly describes a big, heavily built body.
Sturdy means much the same, so it is not the opposite.
Defiant and disagreeable are about behaviour, not build.
The answer is slight.

ex.main: **Slight.** Both words describe a build, which is why slight is the true opposite — narrow and light where burly is broad and heavy. The other two describe how someone acts.
ex.tip: A slight frame, a burly frame — same category, opposite ends.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of companion?
questions.hint: Com- means with, and -pan is bread. A companion is someone you share a meal with.
steps: A companion is someone who is on your side.
Partner means the same, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is someone working against you.
The answer is foe.

ex.main: **Foe.** A companion goes along with you; a foe works against you. Walker and barrier name a person and a thing, but neither is about being for or against you.
ex.tip: All four are nouns on purpose — you cannot rule any out by its form.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of compatible?
questions.hint: Com- means together. Compatible is about how well two things go together.
steps: Compatible people get along without friction.
Cooperative means much the same, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is someone who makes getting along hard.
The answer is disagreeable.

ex.main: **Disagreeable.** Compatible is about two people fitting together easily; disagreeable is about one who argues with everything. Inattentive is about attention, not agreement.
ex.tip: Compatible and patient share a root that means to bear or put up with.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of concept?
questions.hint: Con- means together and -cept means taken. A concept is an idea still taking shape in your head.
steps: A concept is an idea somebody is still working out.
Notion means the same, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is something already settled and proven.
The answer is fact.

ex.main: **Fact.** A concept is still being thought through; a fact has already been checked and proven. That gap between thought-about and proven is what makes them opposites.
ex.tip: Notion is a SYNONYM of concept, sitting there to catch a fast read.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of distract?
questions.hint: Dis- means away and -tract means pull, as in tractor. Distract pulls you away.
steps: To distract is to pull attention away from what someone is doing.
Divert means the same, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is pulling attention back to one place.
The answer is focus.

ex.main: **Focus.** Distract scatters attention outward; focus gathers it onto one thing. They are opposite directions for the same thing — where your attention goes.
ex.tip: Divert is a SYNONYM of distract.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of obedient?
questions.hint: Ob- means to and the rest comes from the Latin for hear — the same root as audio.
steps: Obedient means doing what you are told.
Dutiful means much the same, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is refusing outright.
The answer is defiant.

ex.main: **Defiant.** Obedient does what it is asked; defiant refuses on purpose. Inattentive is not refusing — it just never heard the instruction, which is a different failure.
ex.tip: That inattentive-versus-defiant difference is worth knowing: one is not listening, the other is saying no.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of obstacle?
questions.hint: Ob- means against and -stacle means stand. Something standing in your way.
steps: An obstacle is something in your way that slows you down.
A hurdle is the same idea, so it is not the opposite.
The opposite is something that helps you along instead.
The answer is advantage.

ex.main: **Advantage.** An obstacle costs you ground; an advantage gains you some. A foe is a person who opposes you, which is not the same as a thing in your path.
ex.tip: Hurdle is a SYNONYM of obstacle — both are things to get over.

questions.q: As an ADJECTIVE, which word means the OPPOSITE of patient?
questions.hint: The trap here does exactly what a patient person does. The answer does the opposite.
steps: As an adjective, patient means willing to wait calmly without fuss.
Someone who waits is being patient, so that is not the opposite.
The opposite is the person who will not wait quietly and says so.
The answer is complains.

ex.main: **Complains.** Patient means waiting calmly; the impatient person is the one grumbling about the wait. Waits is what a patient person actually does, which is why it is the trap.
ex.tip: Your sheet gives this antonym as a verb form rather than an adjective — unusual, but that is what it says, so that is what the test will want.

questions.q: Grandma retired at nine and slept soundly. Which words mean the OPPOSITE of retire?
questions.hint: The sentence tells you which meaning of retire is in play. Think about what happens the next morning.
steps: In this sentence retire means going to bed for the night.
Quit and stop are synonyms for that, so they are not the opposite.
The opposite of going to bed is getting up again.
The answer is rise, wake.

ex.main: **Rise, wake.** Retire has more than one meaning, so the sentence does the deciding: here it is turning in for the night, and its opposite is getting up. Quit and stop mean the same as retire, not the opposite.
ex.tip: Retire comes from re- (back) plus the French tirer, to draw — to draw yourself back.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as jostle?
questions.hint: Jostle is a cousin of joust — picture knights knocking into each other.
steps: To jostle is to push and knock against people around you.
Budge is only moving a little, and it is not about pushing others.
Oppose and focus are not about physical contact at all.
The answer is shove.

ex.main: **Shove.** Jostling is bumping and pushing against other people, which is what a shove is. Budge is the near-miss: it means to move slightly, with no pushing of anyone else.
ex.tip: Your sheet gives no antonym for jostle, so this one is only ever asked as a match.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as pedestrian?
questions.hint: Ped- means foot — the same root as pedal and pedicure.
steps: All four of these name a person, so the form does not help.
Companion, foe and partner describe how someone relates to you.
Pedestrian describes how someone is travelling — on foot.
The answer is walker.

ex.main: **Walker.** All four name a person, so you have to know the word itself: pedestrian is about HOW someone is getting around, on foot, while the other three are about who they are to you.
ex.tip: Hiker works too. Your sheet gives no antonym for pedestrian.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as companion?
questions.hint: One of these is the word’s OPPOSITE, not a match for it. Read the question again before you pick.
steps: A companion is someone who goes along with you.
Foe is the opposite of that, so it is not a match.
Walker and barrier are about travel and blocking, not company.
The answer is partner.

ex.main: **Partner.** A companion and a partner are both someone alongside you. Foe is there because it is companion’s OPPOSITE — easy to grab if you read the question too fast.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as obstacle?
questions.hint: One of these is the word’s OPPOSITE, not a match for it. Read the question again before you pick.
steps: An obstacle is something standing in your way.
Advantage is the opposite of that, so it is not a match.
A foe is a person, not a thing in your path.
The answer is barrier.

ex.main: **Barrier.** Both are things blocking the way forward. Advantage is obstacle’s opposite, sitting there to catch a fast read, and a foe is a person rather than a thing in your path.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as concept?
questions.hint: One of these is the word’s OPPOSITE, not a match for it. Read the question again before you pick.
steps: A concept is something you are still thinking through.
A fact is already proven, which makes it the opposite.
Barrier and advantage are about your path, not your thinking.
The answer is idea.

ex.main: **Idea.** A concept is a thought being worked out, which is exactly what an idea is. Fact is the trap — it is concept’s opposite, because a fact is settled and a concept is not.

questions.q: Grandpa yawned and said he was ready to retire. Which word means almost the same as retire?
questions.hint: The sentence sets the meaning. Two of these are what he would do the NEXT morning.
steps: In this sentence retire means stopping for the day.
Rise and wake are what you do after that, so they are opposites.
Budge means to move slightly, which is unrelated.
The answer is quit.

ex.main: **Quit.** Here retire means calling it a day and stopping. Rise and wake are the trap: they are retire’s opposites, so they belong to the other kind of question.
ex.tip: Stop, turn in and call it a day all work too.
